projects.name: TaskNexus
projects.summary: An evolving work-execution platform spanning client/freelancer tasks, developer profiles, people and team discovery, team-owned projects, contributions, hackathons and early-career opportunities.
projects.problem: Freelancers and clients manage briefs, delivery and proof across disconnected systems. Students and builders struggle to discover collaborators, demonstrate what they actually contributed, organize hackathon teams and discover credible early-career opportunities.
projects.product_idea_and_motivation: Original version: connect clients with skilled freelancers and track paid-task workflows. V2 direction: CONNECT → BUILD → PROVE → GROW, linking skills and people discovery to Teams, team Projects, project tasks, verifiable contributions and public showcases. Newer platform phases also integrate hackathons, organizations and internships. The longer-term TaskNexus AI vision is an execution layer, not simply a chatbot or freelance marketplace.
implemented_or_documented_features: Client and freelancer dashboards, marketplace task briefs, acceptance, progress, submissions, revisions and review
Participant-only marketplace task workspace with Overview, Work, Delivery, Discussion and Activity
Professional profiles with canonical skills, availability, visibility and user opt-in
Deterministic people discovery; no opaque ranking or AI quality score
Team creation, contextual owner/admin/member roles, openings, membership and collaboration requests
Team-owned projects, scoped participants, project tasks, milestones and activity
Evidence ledger for participation, roles, task completions and optional external GitHub commits/PRs
Privacy-safe public project showcases and project proof linked to applications
Hackathon catalog, participant discovery, team registration and deadline-bound submissions
Early-career opportunity catalog, organization profiles, eligibility explanations and applications
Phase 9 context-aware organization recruiter workspace and native application pipeline
Notifications, search/command palette, onboarding, user/account administration and security controls
user_workflow: A developer creates a profile with skills and chooses whether to be discoverable.
They find people or a public team opening and send an explicit collaboration request.
A team forms and creates a project with milestones and project tasks.
Members complete assigned work; the system records attributed, verifiable evidence.
A completed project can publish a privacy-safe showcase and support job or internship applications.
For client work, a client posts a task, an eligible freelancer accepts it, progress is updated and delivery is reviewed in a separate marketplace lifecycle.

architecture.current_main_branch: React/Vite frontend → Express API → MongoDB Atlas/Mongoose; short-lived memory-held access tokens; rotating HttpOnly refresh-token cookie; authenticated SSE; service/repository/data-layer boundaries; audited admin provisioning; backend-controlled RBAC and visibility.
domain_separation: Marketplace tasks are different entities from team project tasks.
User account roles are distinct from contextual team and organization roles.

faq.question: What is TaskNexus?
alternate_phrasings: What is his basic idea for TaskNexus?
faq.answer: TaskNexus is an evolving work and collaboration platform. Its original business model connected clients and freelancers for task briefs, progress and delivery. V2 adds professional profiles, discovery, contextual Teams, team-owned Projects, project tasks, factual contribution evidence, public showcases, hackathons and early-career opportunities. Its long-term north star is CONNECT → BUILD → PROVE → GROW.

faq.question: What is Gaurav's original idea for TaskNexus?
faq.answer: The initial idea was a service/task outsourcing platform: a client submits a work requirement, a freelancer accepts eligible work, completion is tracked, submissions are reviewed and administrators govern the process. Over time Gaurav expanded it into a developer network that helps people connect, build in teams, create inspectable contribution evidence and discover future opportunities.

faq.question: Why did he change TaskNexus's vision?
faq.answer: A pure task marketplace did not fully address the journey from meeting collaborators to building something meaningful and demonstrating who contributed. V2 connects profiles, Team membership, Projects, work records and proof to opportunities, while retaining marketplace task flows as a separate bounded domain.

faq.question: What does CONNECT → BUILD → PROVE → GROW mean?
faq.answer: CONNECT: discover people, skills and teams with explicit visibility. BUILD: work in Teams and Projects with milestones and tasks. PROVE: record factual contribution events and publish selected showcases. GROW: use those verified public accomplishments when pursuing hackathons, internships and other opportunities.

faq.question: What features are already in TaskNexus V2?
faq.answer: The public main README documents client/freelancer task flows, professional profiles, deterministic people discovery, contextual Team roles/openings, Team Projects and tasks, contribution evidence, public showcases, hackathon participation, early-career opportunities, application tracking, notifications and admin operations. Existence in the repository is not proof of current production availability.

faq.question: How does TaskNexus work end to end?
faq.answer: A builder creates a professional profile, opts into discovery and contacts a team. Team owners create Projects, invite contributors and organize project tasks. When work is completed, the system can record evidence with attribution; selected completed work becomes a public showcase. Users can refer to public proof when applying for opportunities. The separate marketplace path lets clients post tasks and freelancers complete and submit them for review.

faq.question: Is TaskNexus a freelance marketplace?
faq.answer: It includes an older bounded client–freelancer task domain, but the broader V2 direction is more than a freelancer marketplace: it also supports developers, Teams, Projects, contribution proof, hackathons and opportunities. Marketplace tasks and project tasks are deliberately separate entities.

faq.question: How are a Team and a Project different in TaskNexus?
faq.answer: A Team is the collaboration group with contextual membership and owner/admin/member permissions. A Project is a specific body of work owned by a Team, with participants, milestones, project tasks and evidence. One Team can organize multiple Projects, and project participation can have its own scoped authorization.

faq.question: How do marketplace tasks differ from project tasks?
faq.answer: Marketplace tasks belong to the client/freelancer outsourcing lifecycle, including acceptance, progress, submission/revision and approval. Project tasks exist within Team-owned Projects and feed into contributor participation and evidence. They must not be renamed, merged or treated as one authorization model.

faq.question: How does TaskNexus prove developers' contributions?
faq.answer: It records factual evidence such as project roles, project participation, completed project tasks and optionally linked public GitHub commits/PRs. Evidence includes attribution, origin, verification level and lifecycle state (active/revoked/superseded). It shows facts and counts rather than an opaque developer quality score.

faq.question: How does TaskNexus find team members?
faq.answer: Current People Discovery is deterministic, not AI ranking. Developers explicitly opt into a public discoverable profile, and searches filter structured fields like skills, roles and availability while respecting blocking and privacy. Team openings use contextual candidate interest and do not auto-grant membership.

faq.question: Does TaskNexus have AI matching now?
faq.answer: The verified main README and discovery documentation do not claim deployed AI ranking or matching. They describe deterministic discovery. AI-driven matching is a future concept in TaskNexus AI plans and should not be presented as live functionality.

faq.question: What is TaskNexus AI?
faq.answer: TaskNexus AI is a proposed phone-friendly execution layer: a user explains an idea naturally or by voice, AI extracts requirements and breaks them into project tasks/milestones, and the existing platform manages execution. The iQOO Hackathon pitch also envisioned context-sensitive talent suggestions and project health insights. This concept is distinct from the verified main product and was not established as fully released.

faq.question: What is the future roadmap for TaskNexus?
alternate_phrasings: What does Gaurav want to add to TaskNexus?
faq.answer: Near-term AI proposal: voice-to-project, requirements extraction, structured task breakdown and phone-first usage. Next-stage research: talent matching, project-health prediction, camera/document understanding and practical offline intelligence. Longer-term research: team intelligence, automated reporting, multilingual voice and advanced risk prediction. Operationally, the established V2 app also needs production backup/restore, monitoring and deployment evidence before declaring launch-ready.

faq.question: Does TaskNexus use PostgreSQL or MongoDB?
faq.answer: The current public TaskNexus main-branch README documents MongoDB Atlas with Mongoose. A separate iQOO hackathon concept presentation mentioned PostgreSQL/Supabase as a possible stack, but that proposal should not replace the verified main application architecture.

faq.question: Does TaskNexus support real payments or escrow?
faq.answer: No real payment gateway or escrow is confirmed in the current main README. Payment records are workflow data, and commercial payment integration is explicitly outside the verified implemented scope.

faq.question: Is TaskNexus publicly launched and production ready?
faq.answer: The last reviewed Phase 11 launch-stabilization report says repository-side hardening was implemented but production readiness remained blocked by external Atlas backup/restore, monitoring, operator ownership and deployed staging evidence. No public production launch should be asserted from that report alone.

faq.question: What is ConnectifyX?
faq.answer: ConnectifyX is Gaurav's multi-portal campus placement and recruitment SaaS. It has College, Student, Recruiter, Admin and Super Admin portals, with batch management, CSV imports, placement drives, student/recruiter workflows, broadcasts and placement reporting. This description is based on his development reports rather than a verified public personal repository.

faq.question: What database does ConnectifyX use?

faq.question: What is MealKhata?
faq.answer: MealKhata is a private hostel/group meal and monthly accounts app. It tracks members, rooms and stays, morning/night meal records, expenses, payments, calculated balances and formal month closing. Its security model uses an owner-provisioned Super Admin and an empty initial database, not fixed demo students.

faq.question: How does MealKhata calculate bills?
faq.answer: The product models daily meal consumption, approved rates, payments and shared expenses, calculating bills in integer paise to avoid floating-point rounding errors. An auditable ledger and settlement validation support month closing and exports.

faq.question: Does MealKhata have hardcoded students?
faq.answer: Its v3 README explicitly says no built-in students and no demo data. A real owner creates the first Super Admin securely, then manages students, administrators, meals, rooms and financial records through the application.

faq.question: How is SmartMess different from MealKhata?
faq.answer: SmartMess focuses on the shared hostel mess experience: menus, attendance, complaints, ratings and admin feedback analytics. MealKhata focuses on private member-based meal scheduling, room stays, financial ledgers, monthly billing and settlements. The two projects address related but different problems.

faq.question: What is InstaX built with?
faq.answer: InstaX is a Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript social-media application backed by Prisma and Neon PostgreSQL, with Clerk identity and UploadThing media handling documented in the newer project description. It includes posts, likes, comments, follows, explore/search and optimistic interactions.

faq.question: What is InsightAudio?
faq.answer: InsightAudio ingests YouTube videos or uploaded recordings, extracts and transcribes audio, generates structured summaries/action points and supports follow-up questions through RAG over the transcript. Its stack includes Python, Streamlit, Whisper, FFmpeg, embedding tools and ChromaDB.

faq.question: How is InsightAudio different from the RAG Teaching Assistant?
faq.answer: InsightAudio focuses on meetings and general recorded videos, with summaries, tasks and queryable memory. The RAG Teaching Assistant specifically indexes course lecture videos and prioritizes grounding answers in the correct lecture title and timestamp. Both use transcription and retrieval, but their user goals differ.

faq.question: What is the Flipkart churn prediction project?
faq.answer: It is an IIT Mandi × Masai educational capstone called Flipkart E-commerce Decision Intelligence. It uses a **synthetic generator**, not actual Flipkart customer data, to demonstrate hypothesis testing, regression, classification, threshold analysis, KNN, clustering/PCA and ensemble models. Any metrics are from a practice dataset and must not be presented as Flipkart business findings.

faq.question: What is the RAG-Based AI Teaching Assistant?
faq.answer: It converts long course videos into a queryable transcript knowledge base. FFmpeg and Whisper produce timestamped text, chunks are merged and embedded for semantic search, and a model answers student questions using retrieved lecture content with video/title/time references.

faq.question: What is TrueCert?
faq.answer: TrueCert is a certificate issuance and verification system. Authorized issuers create uniquely identified PDF certificates and QR-based verification URLs; others verify status publicly, including revocation/expiry. It also includes issuance and verification analytics.

faq.question: What is BuildMyTeam?
faq.answer: BuildMyTeam helps college students discover hackathons, create teams, request membership, receive approval and collaborate with project links and notifications. Authorized admins oversee users, teams and events. It focuses on student hackathon team formation, not the broad career/evidence journey of TaskNexus.

faq.question: What is FocusGuard?
faq.answer: FocusGuard is a webcam-based computer-vision productivity prototype that tries to identify sustained phone-related distractions and alerts the user. It uses OpenCV and a YOLO detection component. Its detections are probabilistic, not mind-reading.

faq.question: Can Fire Detection Alert System replace a fire alarm?
faq.answer: No. It is an educational computer-vision prototype using image color, motion and contour checks to identify fire-like signals and sound an alert. It is not a certified life-safety fire alarm or emergency detection system.

faq.question: What is Kanoon-Mate?
faq.answer: Kanoon-Mate is a legal-document accessibility project that uses OCR and an AI language model to simplify Indian legal notices in Hindi and English, highlight possible deadlines and explain referenced law. It is an information tool; users should verify legal interpretations with qualified counsel.

faq.question: What is FreshCart?
faq.answer: FreshCart is a grocery-commerce application with catalog/category browsing, cart/checkout flow, delivery addresses and order/admin workflows described in its repository. Individual integration readiness should be confirmed against the current application.

Tell me the TaskNexus idea Answer: TaskNexus is an evolving work and collaboration platform. Its original business model connected clients and freelancers for task briefs, progress and delivery. V2 adds professional profiles, discovery, contextual Teams, team-owned Projects, project tasks, factual contribution evidence, public showcases, hackathons and early-career opportunities. Its long-term north star is CONNECT → BUILD → PROVE → GROW.

retrieval_records.title: What is Gaurav's original idea for TaskNexus?

retrieval_records.text: Question: What is Gaurav's original idea for TaskNexus? Alternate questions: TaskNexus starting concept Why TaskNexus was created? Answer: The initial idea was a service/task outsourcing platform: a client submits a work requirement, a freelancer accepts eligible work, completion is tracked, submissions are reviewed and administrators govern the process. Over time Gaurav expanded it into a developer network that helps people connect, build in teams, create inspectable contribution evidence and discover future opportunities.

retrieval_records.text: Question: What does CONNECT → BUILD → PROVE → GROW mean? Alternate questions:  Answer: CONNECT: discover people, skills and teams with explicit visibility. Team owners create Projects, invite contributors and organize project tasks. When work is completed, the system can record evidence with attribution; selected completed work becomes a public showcase. Users can refer to public proof when applying for opportunities. The separate marketplace path lets clients post tasks and freelancers complete and submit them for review.

One Team can organize multiple Projects, and project participation can have its own scoped authorization.
